# sequential-analysis

> Python library for sequential statistical inference: tests, confidence sequences and detectors that may be checked after every observation and stopped at any time with their error guarantees intact. Wald's SPRT and Kiefer-Weiss optimal plans, group sequential designs for clinical trials (O'Brien-Fleming and Pocock alpha spending, futility bounds, sample sizes; checked against rpact), anytime-valid A/B tests with e-values and confidence sequences (conversion, bounded and rate metrics, sample ratio mismatch, e-BH false discovery rate control), change-point detection (CUSUM, Shiryaev-Roberts, nonparametric e-detectors, Bayesian online change points), Kalman, particle and hidden Markov filters, forecasting and GARCH volatility. Runs are checkpointed as JSON and resumed bit for bit; a TypeScript executor continues the same checkpoints.

- Install: `pip install sequential-analysis`; import: `sequential_analysis`. Python 3.8 or later, no required dependencies (numpy optional).
- Each procedure states its guarantee in its `guarantee` attribute: exact, asymptotic, model, approximate or none.
- Licence: AGPL-3.0, or a commercial licence from Novikov Laboratories LLC (andrei@hobukob.ru).
- Source: https://github.com/andre-a-no/sequential-analysis. PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/sequential-analysis/

The whole documentation in one file, without the API reference: https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/llms-full.txt

## User guide

- [Overview](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/): the library in one paragraph and the questions the guide answers
- [Why can't I look at a p-value every day?](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/peeking/): the peeking problem, measured, and the three families of sequential methods
- [Stop an A/B test early](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/ab-testing/): TwoProportionTest, BoundedABTest, SampleRatioMismatch, MultipleTests
- [Confidence intervals you can monitor](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/confidence-sequences/): confidence sequences for bounded means, quantiles and heavy-tailed data
- [Wald's SPRT in Python](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/sprt/): SPRT, TwoSPRT, Kiefer-Weiss plans
- [Interim analyses of a clinical trial](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/clinical-trials/): group_sequential_design, alpha spending, sample sizes
- [Detect a change in a stream](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/change-detection/): CUSUM, e-detectors, choosing the ARL
- [Streams, checkpoints and crashes](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/streaming/): Run, Delivery, Run.restore, history digest
- [Compared with other libraries](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/comparison/): statsmodels, rpact, gsDesign, confseq, safestats, ruptures, filterpy, arch, hmmlearn
- [Frequently asked questions](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/faq/): licence, production use, power, speed, citing
- [Glossary](https://andre-a-no.github.io/sequential-analysis/guide/glossary/): e-value, confidence sequence, alpha spending, ARL and synonyms
